title: Empirical Bridge Framework
purpose: Establish the governance framework for relating RT Calculus formal structures to empirical observations while preserving the distinction between formal mathematics and measurement.
summary: This patch introduces the concept of an empirical bridge. An empirical bridge is a governed mapping between a formal RT Calculus object and observable phenomena. It is neither proof of the calculus nor a derivation of reality from RT Calculus.

basis.scope: Provisional empirical-bridge witness that introduces a governed correspondence layer between formal RT objects and independently observed phenomena while leaving RT_core unchanged.

core_rule.statement: Empirical bridge correspondences may be introduced only as provisional mappings between formal RT objects and independently defined observables, and they must remain distinct from proof, derivation, or modification of RT_core.

EmpiricalBridge.definition: A governed correspondence between a formal RT Calculus object and one or more empirical observables.

Observable.definition: A measurable quantity, event, pattern, or dataset obtained independently of RT Calculus.

BridgeHypothesis.definition: A provisional claim that a specified empirical observable corresponds to a specified formal RT object.

BridgeEvidence.definition: Evidence supporting or contradicting a BridgeHypothesis without modifying the formal calculus.

formal_reading.interpretation: An empirical bridge is interpretive, not constitutive. The formal object exists independently of the empirical mapping.

governance_rules.rule: No empirical observation may modify RT_core.
Bridge hypotheses are provisional and independently falsifiable.
Failure of a bridge hypothesis does not invalidate the formal calculus unless the bridge was previously promoted to theorem.
Empirical observables must be defined independently of RT terminology.
Multiple competing bridge hypotheses may coexist until evidence discriminates between them.
Bridge evidence updates the status of the bridge hypothesis only; it does not rewrite formal objects.

forbidden_inferences: An empirical bridge is not proof of RT Calculus.
A successful bridge does not imply uniqueness.
A failed bridge does not falsify RT_core.
Correlation alone does not establish a bridge.
Bridge hypotheses do not become theorems through repeated observation alone.

required_repo_changes.description: Add the empirical-bridge framework witness that defines EB as a governed correspondence layer.
Add example bridge hypotheses and observations that show the separation between formal calculus and empirical mapping.
Add counterexamples that block proof, derivation, uniqueness, and calculus-modification readings of EB.
Register the new documentation surfaces and patch record by hash for governance visibility.

acceptance_tests.test: A bridge hypothesis can be created without modifying RT_core.
Contradictory evidence changes bridge status but leaves formal calculus unchanged.
Multiple bridge hypotheses may reference the same formal object without governance conflict.
Bridge observables are defined independently of RT Calculus notation.

success_criteria: The patch remains additive and leaves RT_core unchanged.
The patch defines an empirical bridge as interpretive rather than constitutive.
Bridge hypotheses remain provisional and falsifiable.
Multiple bridge hypotheses may coexist without conflict.
Bridge evidence can update bridge status without rewriting the formal calculus.

textbook_integration.integration_note: Introduce empirical bridges as an interpretive layer above the formal calculus, explicitly separating mathematical structure from experimental application.

governance_notes: This patch begins a new campaign focused on empirical interpretation.
It preserves the independence of the formal calculus from experimental evidence.

next_expected_patch.title: Bridge Evaluation Protocol
next_expected_patch.purpose: Define standardized procedures for proposing, testing, scoring, and retiring empirical bridge hypotheses.
